thread:
Maria: heads-up — quick design check on the API keys drawer I mocked this morning. main concerns: focus order, empty-state affordance, and how revoke/undo is surfaced. screenshot: https://img.redwood.local/mock/key-drawer-1.png

AJ: looks promising. couple quick q's: 1) where should the primary CTA live in the drawer — top-right like current, or sticky bottom-right? 2) revoke undo — ephemeral toast or inline reversible state? :thinking:

Sam: +1 on focus concerns. when drawer opens keyboard focus should land on the first actionable element (probably the list when keys exist, or the create button for empty). ESC should close, Tab should loop inside (focus-trap).

Irina: accessibility nit: the revoke confirmation modal currently uses generic copy. propose: `Revoke key? This will immediately stop all requests using this key.` add `aria-describedby` pointing to that sentence. Undo toast should be `aria-live=polite` and include a 10s window.

AJ: for CTA placement — my preference is bottom-right sticky if the drawer can be long (keeps create always reachable). top-right works for short drawers. Also prefer the primary CTA to be verb-first: `Create API key` instead of just `Create`.

Maria: agreed on verb-first. proposed empty-state copy: "No API keys yet — create one to get started." microcopy under CTA: "You can limit this key to specific models and routes later." less scary than full perms explanation.

Sam: suggestion on revoke flow: instead of destructive modal + toast, consider inline soft-delete where the row collapses into a pale banner: `Key revoked — undo` for 10s. better context and fewer full-screen interruptions.

Irina: inline soft-delete helps muscle memory, but make sure screen readers announce the change. Banner should have role="status" and `aria-live="assertive"` maybe polite? might be assertive if it blocks functionality. test with NVDA.

AJ: copy proposals (quick snippets):
```
Primary button: "Create API key"
Secondary: "Create & download"
Revoke confirmation heading: "Revoke API key"
Revoke body: "This will immediately invalidate the key. Any services using it will stop working."
Undo toast: "Key revoked — undo" (actionable)
```

Maria: love it. small UX nit: `Create & download` sounds like it does 2 steps; maybe `Create and download` reads clearer in high-contrast small-screen contexts. also we need to surface a warning if the user hasn't saved the key elsewhere (download step).

UI-bot: accessibility-check results: focus-trap: FAIL; aria-live for toasts: MISSING; button order mismatch on mobile: FAIL. Uploaded annotated screenshot to the design board: https://design.redwood.local/board/keys-announce

Sam: regarding scopes/perms labels — UX discussion: "Read / Write / Admin" vs "View / Use / Manage". I prefer verbs: `Use` is more accurate for 'can call the API'. `Manage` implies key lifecycle. Thoughts?

Irina: verbs are clearer to non-technical users. maybe two-line hint under scope selector: first line short label (`Use`) second line tiny helper: `Allows using this key to call the API` (12px). keep contrast OK.

AJ: one more layout nit: the key row overflow menu currently puts Revoke below Copy and Rename. Revoke should be visually separated (danger color) and maybe grouped under "Danger" section to avoid accidental taps.

Maria: plan: I'll update prototype — move primary CTA to sticky bottom-right for long drawers, implement inline soft-delete + undo toast with aria-live, change copy to verb-first, and separate revoke in overflow menu. I'll push a new Figma frame by EOD. @AJ can you review copy and @Irina can sanity-check aria attributes?

AJ: sure, I'll review once uploaded. thanks. :thumbsup:

Irina: I'll run quick screen-reader pass after the update.

UI-bot: design assets uploaded: keys-drawer-v2.fig (https://design.redwood.local/file/keys-drawer-v2)
